name: Object-Order Ray-Casting
definition: An efficient and accurate volume rendering technique that combines the speed advantages of object-order methods (optimized volume run, easy space leaping) with the high-quality image generation of ray-casting (trilinear interpolation). It aims to achieve interactive high-quality rendering (up to 10 fps) on current workstations, overcoming the limitations of image-order ray-casting (slow due to cache misses) and object-order methods (low quality or inefficient hidden volume removal).
